source.title: Dorsolateral neostriatum contribution to incentive salience: opioid or dopamine stimulation makes one reward cue more motivationally attractive than another.

confidence_rationale: Microinjection + behaviour showing limbic activation dynamically amplifies attraction toward a previously-learned Pavlovian cue, making it a 'stronger motivational magnet' at the expense of a competing cue, due to stronger motivation (not habit), with sign-trackers flexibly following the cue to a new location. Maps cleanly onto cue_pull as a directional, competing, motivation-driven pull toward the cued object. Docked for rat striatal microinjection and individual-difference dependence (sign- vs goal-trackers).
failure_signatures: The cue-magnet effect was individual-difference dependent (sign-trackers vs goal-trackers) and required limbic drug activation; a uniform cue_pull may not capture this heterogeneity or its state-dependence.
Amplification was selective and competitive (one cue at the expense of another), implying cue_pull should arbitrate across competing cues rather than independently nudge toward each.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Opioid or dopamine stimulation of dorsolateral striatum selectively amplifies the incentive attraction of a previously-learned Pavlovian cue, making it a stronger motivational magnet at the expense of a competing cue, via motivation rather than habit; sign-trackers flexibly track the cue to new locations.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-347's cue_pull as a directional pull toward the strongest-perceived cued object (StepHarness derives the strongest-perceived type from SD-049 per-type proximity); the 'motivational magnet' that competitively dominates other cues matches a z_goal nudge toward the dominant cue without revaluation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Demonstrated via DLS pharmacological stimulation in rats with strong individual differences; REE's cue_pull is a deterministic fixed-gain nudge without a state/dopamine analog and without modelling sign- vs goal-tracker phenotypes, so the competitive arbitration the paper shows is only partially captured.
mapping.source_context: Rats, autoshaping (sign- vs goal-tracking), intra-DLS DAMGO or amphetamine microinjection.

confidence_components.notes: Behaviourally direct cue-pull analog; transfer risk elevated by rodent pharmacology and phenotype-dependence.
